goal: Diagnose the preserved Local Project Board Provider timeout and concurrency shortfall, then correct only confirmed transport telemetry and fallback-observability defects.
acceptance_criteria: The original failed production run and every passing Provider leaf remain intact.
Two production-client attempts and one minimal-client attempt use the same reconstructed logical payload with a recorded request hash and no credential disclosure.
Transport telemetry distinguishes request size, response-header receipt, response-body receipt, and total elapsed time without changing retry or timeout policy.
An API-only timeout records fallback consideration but cannot claim local fallback execution or reduce Provider leaf concurrency.
The 16-job DAG, real waves, timestamps, concurrency ceiling, critical path, and fragmentation cost are reported without changing the Planner or adding a scheduler.

quality_metrics.target: the existing production Provider client and sole leaf scheduler remain authoritative
quality_metrics.method: kernel contract inspection and focused routing regressions

quality_metrics.target: all focused transport, routing, ProviderJob, and kernel tests pass
quality_metrics.method: targeted pytest profile and slim rule guard

prevention: Keep request identity and timing telemetry redacted and thread-local.
assurance: Compare the production transport with an independent minimal client against one byte-identical isolation payload.
control: Reproduce twice with retry disabled, inspect original phase timestamps, and run focused regressions.
improvement: Defer ProviderJob regrouping to a separate reviewed increment after recording the measured fragmentation evidence.

interface_expectations: scripts/run_local_pipeline_impl.py continues to own the sole production Provider leaf worker pool.
scripts/check_connectivity.py retains the existing OpenAI-compatible request route and timeout policy.
No supervision, router, authority, evidence, packaging, or delivery contract changes are made.

feedback: Both production attempts and the minimal client timed out before response headers on the same 27,536-byte payload, while a small control request passed in 8.61 seconds.
The Provider/model is reachable, but the failed CSS request remains over the 90-second bound, so operational resume was correctly not attempted.
A misleading fallback event had reduced later leaf worker counts despite zero local-model invocation; the event semantics and regression now prevent that reduction.

worked: Preserved run artifacts and event timestamps were sufficient to reconstruct the DAG and expose the false fallback-to-concurrency coupling.
did_not_work: Historical telemetry did not retain request bodies, response-phase timing, or request ids, so the original bytes could not be replayed exactly.
experiments: The reconstructed payload differed by 91 prompt characters from the first historical attempt but was byte-identical across isolation tests A, B, and C.
